views.name: sales_facts_2020_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  rowid AS sale_id,
  product_code AS product_id,
  date AS sale_date,
  sold_quantity || '|' || customer_code || '|' || fiscal_year AS other_sale_fields_optional
FROM hardware_fact_sales_monthly
WHERE date >= '2020-01-01' AND date <= '2020-12-01'
views.description: All sales fact rows whose sale date falls in calendar year 2020. This is a filtered cohort of sales events used to identify products that had sales in 2020.

views.name: sales_facts_2021_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  rowid AS sale_id,
  product_code AS product_id,
  date AS sale_date,
  json_object(
    'customer_code', customer_code,
    'sold_quantity', sold_quantity,
    'fiscal_year', fiscal_year
  ) AS other_sale_fields_optional
FROM hardware_fact_sales_monthly
WHERE date >= '2021-01-01' AND date <= '2021-12-31'
views.description: All sales fact rows whose sale date falls in calendar year 2021. This is a filtered cohort of sales events used to identify products that had sales in 2021.

views.name: product_catalog_hardware_segments
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_code AS product_id,
  segment AS hardware_product_segment
FROM hardware_dim_product
WHERE segment IS NOT NULL
  AND segment != ''
views.description: Product catalog rows restricted to products classified as hardware product segments; exposes product identifier and its hardware segment attribute for grouping.

views.name: unique_products_per_segment_by_year
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pcs.hardware_product_segment AS hardware_product_segment,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN hf.fiscal_year = 2020 THEN p.product_code END) AS unique_products_2020,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN hf.fiscal_year = 2021 THEN p.product_code END) AS unique_products_2021,
  p.product_code AS product_code,
  hf.date AS date,
  hf.product_code AS hf_product_code,
  hf.customer_code AS customer_code,
  hf.sold_quantity AS sold_quantity,
  hf.fiscal_year AS fiscal_year
FROM hardware_fact_sales_monthly hf
JOIN hardware_dim_product p
  ON hf.product_code = p.product_code
LEFT JOIN product_catalog_hardware_segments pcs
  ON p.product_code = pcs.product_id
GROUP BY pcs.hardware_product_segment
views.description: For each hardware product segment and product, determine presence in 2020 and 2021 sales cohorts and then aggregate to counts of distinct products per segment for each year. This produces one row per segment with counts for 2020 and 2021 and leaves percentage-change computation to the final combination step.

views.name: sales_2021_hardware
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  hf.rowid AS sale_id,
  hf.date AS sale_date,
  hf.product_code AS product_id,
  pd.product AS product_name,
  pd.division AS division_name,
  pd.division AS division_id,
  hf.sold_quantity AS quantity
FROM hardware_fact_sales_monthly hf
JOIN hardware_dim_product pd
  ON hf.product_code = pd.product_code
WHERE hf.date >= '2021-01-01' AND hf.date <= '2021-12-31'
views.description: All sales rows within the calendar year 2021 that involve products classified as hardware. Keep each sale line with its quantity, product id, product name (if available), sale date, and division (the division associated with the sale or the product depending on schema).

views.name: product_quantity_by_division
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.division AS division_id,
  p.division AS division_name,
  h.product_code AS product_id,
  h.product AS product_name,
  SUM(f.sold_quantity) AS total_quantity_2021
FROM hardware_fact_sales_monthly f
JOIN hardware_dim_product h
  ON f.product_code = h.product_code
JOIN hardware_dim_product p
  ON h.product_code = p.product_code
WHERE f.fiscal_year = 2021
GROUP BY p.division, h.product_code, h.product
views.description: Total quantity sold in 2021 per product within each division. Sum quantities from the sales cohort to produce one row per product+division with the product-level total quantity for the year.

views.name: product_rank_within_division
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.division AS division_id,
  p.division AS division_name,
  p.product_code AS product_id,
  p.product AS product_name,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN hf.fiscal_year = 2021 THEN hf.sold_quantity END), 0) AS total_quantity_2021,
  RANK() OVER (
    PARTITION BY p.division
    ORDER BY COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN hf.fiscal_year = 2021 THEN hf.sold_quantity END), 0) DESC
  ) AS product_rank_in_division
FROM hardware_dim_product p
LEFT JOIN hardware_fact_sales_monthly hf
  ON p.product_code = hf.product_code
GROUP BY p.division, p.product_code, p.product
views.description: Rank products within each division by their 2021 total_quantity (descending). Preserve one row per product+division with its rank to identify the top products per division.

views.name: avg_quantity_top3_per_division
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  hd.division AS division_id,
  hd.division AS division_name,
  AVG(sub.total_quantity_2021) AS average_quantity_top3
FROM hardware_dim_product hd
JOIN (
  SELECT
    hp.product_code,
    hp.division,
    SUM(hf.sold_quantity) AS total_quantity_2021,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY hp.division ORDER BY SUM(hf.sold_quantity) DESC) AS product_rank_in_division
  FROM hardware_dim_product hp
  JOIN hardware_fact_sales_monthly hf
    ON hp.product_code = hf.product_code
    AND hf.fiscal_year = 2021
  GROUP BY hp.product_code, hp.division
) sub
  ON hd.product_code = sub.product_code
  AND hd.division = sub.division
WHERE sub.product_rank_in_division <= 3
GROUP BY hd.division
views.description: For each division, take the products whose rank is within the top 3 (i.e., rank <= 3); then compute the arithmetic mean of total_quantity_2021 across those selected products. If a division has fewer than three products, average across however many exist. Produce one row per division with the resulting average.

views.name: web_order_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  web_orders.id AS order_id,
  web_orders.occurred_at AS order_date,
  web_orders.total_amt_usd AS order_amount,
  web_accounts.sales_rep_id AS sales_rep_id,
  web_reps.region_id AS region_id
FROM web_orders
JOIN web_accounts ON web_orders.account_id = web_accounts.id
JOIN web_sales_reps AS web_reps ON web_accounts.sales_rep_id = web_reps.id
JOIN web_events ON web_events.account_id = web_accounts.id AND web_events.occurred_at = web_orders.occurred_at
WHERE web_events.channel = 'direct'
views.description: Select all order rows that are web sales (restrict to the web sales channel). Include order identifier, order date, order amount, sales representative identifier, and region identifier for each web order row.

views.name: region_order_counts_and_totals
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  wr.region_id AS region_id,
  COUNT(wr.order_id) AS order_count,
  SUM(wr.order_amount) AS region_total_sales
FROM web_order_rows wr
GROUP BY wr.region_id
views.description: Aggregate the web_order_rows to compute per-region metrics: count of web orders and sum of web order amounts (region total sales).

views.name: rep_region_sales
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  wr.region_id AS region_id,
  wr.sales_rep_id AS sales_rep_id,
  SUM(wr.order_amount) AS rep_region_sales
FROM web_order_rows AS wr
GROUP BY
  wr.region_id,
  wr.sales_rep_id
views.description: From web_order_rows, compute total web sales per sales representative within each region (sum of order_amount grouped by region and sales rep).

views.name: region_top_reps
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  rrs.region_id,
  rrs.sales_rep_id,
  rrs.rep_region_sales AS top_rep_sales
FROM rep_region_sales rrs
JOIN (
  SELECT region_id, MAX(rep_region_sales) AS max_sales
  FROM rep_region_sales
  GROUP BY region_id
) max_per_region
  ON rrs.region_id = max_per_region.region_id
  AND rrs.rep_region_sales = max_per_region.max_sales
views.description: For each region, find the maximum rep_region_sales and return rows for every sales representative whose rep_region_sales equals that per-region maximum; include the rep sales amount. This will produce one row per top representative per region.

views.name: faculty_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  FacRank AS rank,
  FacFirstName AS first_name,
  FacLastName AS last_name,
  FacSalary AS salary,
  FacNo AS faculty_id
FROM university_faculty
views.description: Select the relevant faculty rows with their rank, first name, last name, and salary (one row per faculty member).

views.name: avg_salary_per_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  FacRank AS rank,
  AVG(FacSalary) AS avg_salary
FROM university_faculty
GROUP BY FacRank
views.description: Compute the average salary for each faculty rank across all faculty members of that rank.

views.name: salary_diff_per_member
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  uf.FacNo AS faculty_member,
  uf.FacRank AS rank,
  uf.FacFirstName AS first_name,
  uf.FacLastName AS last_name,
  uf.FacSalary AS salary,
  avg_rank.avg_salary AS avg_salary,
  ABS(uf.FacSalary - avg_rank.avg_salary) AS abs_diff
FROM university_faculty AS uf
JOIN (
  SELECT
    FacRank AS rank,
    AVG(FacSalary) AS avg_salary
  FROM university_faculty
  GROUP BY FacRank
) AS avg_rank
  ON uf.FacRank = avg_rank.rank
views.description: Join each faculty member to their rank's average salary and compute the absolute difference between the member's salary and the rank average.

views.name: closest_to_avg_per_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.rank AS rank,
  s.first_name AS first_name,
  s.last_name AS last_name,
  s.salary AS salary
FROM salary_diff_per_member s
JOIN (
  SELECT rank, MIN(abs_diff) AS min_abs_diff
  FROM salary_diff_per_member
  GROUP BY rank
) m
  ON s.rank = m.rank
  AND s.abs_diff = m.min_abs_diff
views.description: For each rank, find the minimal absolute difference (distance) between member salary and the rank average, and return the faculty members whose abs_diff equals that minimal value (include ties).

views.name: raw_rows_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "index" AS row_id,
  CompanyName AS company,
  Location AS location,
  Salary AS salary_raw,
  json_object(
    'JobTitle', JobTitle,
    'SalariesReported', SalariesReported
  ) AS other_source_columns
FROM SalaryDataset
WHERE Location IN ('Mumbai','Pune','New Delhi','Hyderabad')
  AND Salary IS NOT NULL
views.description: Select the source rows restricted to the four target cities and non-null salary field values (no cleaning yet). This is the raw cohort of rows we will clean and aggregate from.

views.name: salary_cleaning
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  rr.row_id AS row_id,
  rr.company AS company,
  rr.location AS location,
  -- remove any non-digit characters; SQLite doesn't have regexp_replace by default,
  -- so iteratively remove common non-digit symbols: currency symbols, commas, slashes, spaces, non-breaking space
  NULLIF(
    CASE
      WHEN trim(rr.salary_raw) = '' OR rr.salary_raw IS NULL THEN NULL
      ELSE
        -- replace common separators and currency marks with empty string using nested REPLACE
        REPLACE(
          REPLACE(
            REPLACE(
              REPLACE(
                REPLACE(
                  REPLACE(rr.salary_raw, '₹', ''),
                'Rs.', ''),
              'Rs', ''),
            ',', ''),
          '/yr', ''),
        ' ', '')
    END
  , '') AS salary_str,
  -- cast the cleaned string to numeric; SQLite will produce NULL if not numeric
  CAST(
    NULLIF(
      CASE
        WHEN trim(rr.salary_raw) = '' OR rr.salary_raw IS NULL THEN NULL
        ELSE
          REPLACE(
            REPLACE(
              REPLACE(
                REPLACE(
                  REPLACE(
                    REPLACE(rr.salary_raw, '₹', ''),
                  'Rs.', ''),
                'Rs', ''),
              ',', ''),
            '/yr', ''),
          ' ', '')
      END
    , '') AS NUMERIC) AS salary_num,
  -- flag true if cast produced a non-NULL numeric value, else false
  CASE WHEN CAST(
    NULLIF(
      CASE
        WHEN trim(rr.salary_raw) = '' OR rr.salary_raw IS NULL THEN NULL
        ELSE
          REPLACE(
            REPLACE(
              REPLACE(
                REPLACE(
                  REPLACE(
                    REPLACE(rr.salary_raw, '₹', ''),
                  'Rs.', ''),
                'Rs', ''),
              ',', ''),
            '/yr', ''),
          ' ', '')
      END
    , '') AS NUMERIC) IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS salary_valid_flag
FROM raw_rows_cohort rr
views.description: Normalize/clean the salary text by removing non-numeric characters and converting to a numeric type. Produce a numeric salary value and a flag indicating successful conversion; keep original row identifiers, company and location.

views.name: company_location_avg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  CompanyName AS company,
  Location AS location,
  AVG(CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(Salary, '₹', ''), ',', ''), '/yr', ''), '/ year', '') AS REAL)) AS avg_salary_location,
  COUNT(*) AS count_rows_location
FROM SalaryDataset
WHERE TRIM(Salary) != ''
  AND CAST(
        REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(Salary, '₹', ''), ',', ''), '/yr', ''), '/ year', '')
      AS REAL) IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY CompanyName, Location
views.description: Compute the average of cleaned numeric salaries per company within each location, considering only rows where the cleaned salary is valid. One row per company-location pair.

views.name: national_avg_and_top5_per_location
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cl.location AS location,
  cl.company AS company,
  cl.avg_salary_location AS avg_salary_location,
  (SELECT AVG(salary_num) FROM salary_cleaning WHERE salary_valid_flag = 1) AS national_avg_salary,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY cl.location ORDER BY cl.avg_salary_location DESC) AS location_rank
FROM company_location_avg cl
views.description: Compute the overall national average salary across all valid cleaned salaries, then for each location keep the top companies ranked by their location-specific average salary. This step attaches the national average to each company-location row and ranks companies within each location for later filtering to top-K.
